vrp.simple: Options are cheap compared with how much BANKEX has actually been moving: they price 17.8% a year while the last month realised 22.6%.
vrp.analyst: IV30 - RV21 = -4.8 vol points, 8th percentile of the past year. Since 2024-01-01, IV30 was above the volatility that actually followed over the next 21 sessions on 62% of days: option sellers are usually paid a premium for carrying the risk, and the gap is what that premium looks like today.

skew.simple: Protection against a fall costs more than a bet on a rise, by 1.8 vol points. That gap is normal for BANKEX against the past year.
skew.analyst: 25-delta risk reversal -1.80 vol pts (front month), 31st percentile of the past year. More negative = more demand for downside insurance relative to upside.

oi.simple: For the 2026-12-31 expiry, the biggest pile of call positions is at 75,000 (+5.6% away) and the biggest pile of put positions is at 69,000 (-2.8%). Option sellers defend these levels, so price often slows near them, but they shift as positions change.
oi.analyst: Front-expiry PCR (OI) 0.87; all-expiry OI PCR at the 31st percentile of the past year. Today's change: calls +2,190, puts +1,500 (OI units, i.e. shares or index quantity). A high PCR in India mostly reflects put writing, so it is read as crowding, not as a signal.
